title: SDK 2.x incompatible with box StartOS 0.4.0-beta.9 (start-container has no bind-mount)
description:
Daemons cannot start on-box. Every volume mount fails:

  start-container bind-mount --source /media/startos/volumes/postgres/ --target .../var/lib/postgresql/data --recursive
  error: unrecognized subcommand 'bind-mount'

No volume mounts => postgres/redis/minio/relay all fail health checks in a tight retry loop.

Root cause: SDK 2.x SubContainer.js shells out to 'start-container bind-mount'. The start-container binary on StartOS 0.4.0-beta.9 does not implement that subcommand.

Verified:
- bind-mount present in SDK 2.0.0, 2.0.2, 2.0.4, 2.0.5, 2.0.6, 2.0.7 (all of 2.x)
- ABSENT in 1.5.3, which uses a different mount mechanism
- wisp-startos and keep-startos -- both installed and RUNNING on this box -- pin start-sdk 1.5.3

CLAUDE.md's stated baseline ('SDK = @start9labs/start-sdk 2.0.6 (references already 0.4.x)') is wrong: the working references are on 1.5.3.

1.5.3 does have every API this package uses (addDaemon, addOneshot, runHealthScript, checkPortListening, MultiHost, FileHelper, Mounts/mountVolume, setupInit, setupOnInit, setupBackups, setupInterfaces), so a downgrade is feasible -- signatures may differ.

DECISION NEEDED:
  A) Update StartOS on the box to a build whose start-container has bind-mount -> stay on 2.0.6, no rewrite.
  B) Downgrade package to start-sdk 1.5.3 to match the box and the sibling packages.

Note: the FullProgressTracker livelock (buzz-relay-startos-apw) may be another symptom of running a 2.x SDK against an older OS.
notes: RESOLVED by upgrading StartOS on the box. New build's start-container includes the bind-mount subcommand (verified via 'start-container --help': action, bind-mount, subcontainer, etc). git-info hash now 514af0c2fa076c8b597d9861f882bdb1b3411d9e. All four volumes mount cleanly; full daemon chain starts. Staying on start-sdk 2.0.6, no downgrade needed.
close_reason: Verified on-box 2026-07-24: init completes instantly (setupInit bypass) and full daemon chain starts after StartOS upgrade restored bind-mount. Relay listening on :3000, health probe on :8080.

title: Install hangs: init JS spins at 99% CPU indefinitely
description:
Install of buzz-relay_x86_64.s9pk (gitHash 7e81c39) wedges on-box at 'Initializing...'. Two attempts (00:10Z and 01:04Z on 2026-07-24) each left an orphan LXC container running /usr/lib/startos/init/index.js at 99% CPU with 17h+ accumulated CPU time. Not I/O blocked: 708G disk free, no error output, startd still waiting on the init RPC it sent at 01:04:13Z.

Ruled out so far:
- Module load of the ncc bundle is clean locally (184ms).
- Disk space (708G free on package-data).
- SDK graph.js BFS and exver VersionRangeTable.zip loops are bounded; versionGraph has other: [] so the graph is trivial.
- getDefaultString charsets 'a-z,A-Z,0-9' and 'a-f,0-9' verified correct locally (2000 samples).

Next step: capture a JS stack from the live spinning process via 'node inspect -p <pid>' inside the orphan container before killing it.

Blocks buzz-relay-startos-487 and -e38 (on-box smoke test / e2e).
notes: VERIFIED FIXED on-box 2026-07-24 16:58: 'Initializing... -> Initialization complete.' in seconds, RPC returns result:null, no orphan container, no CPU spin. The setupInit bypass in startos/init/index.ts works.
close_reason: Verified on-box 2026-07-24: init completes instantly (setupInit bypass) and full daemon chain starts after StartOS upgrade restored bind-mount. Relay listening on :3000, health probe on :8080.

title: Set stable relay identity key and enable REST token auth
description: relayEnv sets neither BUZZ_RELAY_PRIVATE_KEY nor BUZZ_REQUIRE_AUTH_TOKEN. The relay binary then falls back to a hardcoded dev keypair (secp256k1 privkey 1, identical on every deployment) and serves REST endpoints with token auth bypassed, on the only public interface (:3000). Generate a 32-byte hex relay key in seedFiles, add to store.json schema, set both env vars. Binary enforces BUZZ_RELAY_PRIVATE_KEY when BUZZ_REQUIRE_AUTH_TOKEN=true, so both must land together.
close_reason: Fixed in 345a2bd: relayPrivateKey generated in seedFiles (CSPRNG 64-char hex), added to store schema and startup validation, BUZZ_RELAY_PRIVATE_KEY and BUZZ_REQUIRE_AUTH_TOKEN=true set in relayEnv. Add-community smoke test tracked in buzz-relay-startos-487.

title: Reset action must also clear MinIO/Redis volumes
description: reset.ts wiped only Postgres, but warning promises full community deletion. MinIO media blobs survived and stayed publicly served at /media; Redis kept stale cache. Wipe minio and redis volumes alongside postgres so reset is a true clean slate.

title: Onboarding: require clearnet Let's Encrypt domain + set-host-before-first-boot flow
description: Start9 community tester (see j8e) hit two invisible failures: (1) Buzz Desktop's wss:// client uses rustls webpki-roots ONLY and ignores the OS/StartOS CA, so a StartOS .local/.onion/private-CA cert fails the WebSocket handshake silently — a PUBLIC clearnet domain with a Let's Encrypt cert is effectively mandatory; (2) the relay permanently binds its community to RELAY_URL's host on first boot with no rename path. Make this impossible to get wrong: surface instructions (init 'properties'/README shown in-UI) stating a public clearnet ACME domain is REQUIRED (Tor/LAN won't work), and that Community Host must equal that domain and be set BEFORE first start. Enforce ordering so the community isn't seeded under the wrong host. Evidence and file:paths in j8e design field.
notes:
Start9 CONFIRMED (2026-08-04): A domain requirement is acceptable for a community package — no need to keep it beta-only waiting on the upstream client-CA fix. And the ACME path is verified to work for Buzz Desktop's webpki-only wss client: if the user chooses Let's Encrypt as the ACME provider AND has port 443 publicly accessible on the IP the domain points to, they reliably get a cert signed by a widely-trusted root (which is exactly what the desktop client's bundled webpki-roots trusts). Onboarding copy must state these two operator preconditions explicitly: (1) select Let's Encrypt as ACME provider, (2) port 443 publicly reachable on the domain's IP.
DRAFT IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-04), not yet committed:
1. Enforcement (startos/main.ts): main now THROWS with an actionable message if store.communityHost is unset, instead of booting the relay with RELAY_URL defaulting to ws://localhost:3000 (which would permanently seed a dead community under host 'localhost:3000'). RELAY_URL / BUZZ_MEDIA_BASE_URL are now set unconditionally after the guard. Configuration action is allowedStatuses:'any' so it stays reachable while the service is stopped on the guard. This is the set-host-before-first-boot enforcement.
2. Onboarding copy (instructions.md): rewrote to require a public clearnet domain, state the two confirmed ACME preconditions (Let's Encrypt provider + public 443 on the domain's IP), explain that .local/.onion won't work (webpki-only client), and warn the host is permanent (no rename/re-point; changing it strands data + NIP-05 identities).
3. Config action copy (startos/actions/config.ts): strengthened communityHost description with the 3 requirements and added a warning field about first-start immutability.
4. i18n: updated ID 20 (communityHost description) + added ID 26 (warning) across default.ts and all 4 translation langs (es/de/fr/pl).
Validated: tsc --noEmit clean; ncc build clean. Immutability copy references resetting the community to move domains — clean 'Reset community' action is c0u (not required for this, reinstall already wipes).
PR opened: https://github.com/privkeyio/buzz-relay-startos/pull/13 (feature/onboarding-domain-enforcement -> master, commit 01e0f0b, signed). Awaiting review/merge. Bead stays in_progress until merged.
Review fix (commit 6a2d5e7): enforce first-start host binding, not just warn. Added store.boundHost; main.ts persists it once on first started boot and always derives RELAY_URL/BUZZ_MEDIA_BASE_URL from boundHost (fallback communityHost); config.ts save handler now rejects any communityHost change once boundHost is set (edits allowed pre-first-start). tsc + ncc clean. Pushed to PR #13.
close_reason: Merged as PR #13 (6f0ebf4): refuse-to-start guard, boundHost first-start lock, config rejection of later host changes, clearnet/Let's Encrypt onboarding copy in instructions.md + config action + README, i18n across 4 langs.

title: tagAndRelease publishing handled by Start9-Community fork (no privkeyio config needed)
description: Resolved: publishing for this package follows the Start9-Community fork model, not privkeyio self-publishing. privkeyio's tagAndRelease.yml fails at the 'Check production registry' step (exit 38) on every master push because privkeyio deliberately has no REFERENCE_REGISTRY/RELEASE_REGISTRY/S3_S9PKS_BASE_URL variables or S3 secrets set — and it should not. Actual publication happens in the Start9-Community fork's CI, which inherits the same unmodified workflow files and runs them green using Start9's org-level secrets/vars. This mirrors the accepted precedent of wisp-startos, where privkeyio's tagAndRelease also fails harmlessly on every push while the Start9-Community fork publishes. No privkeyio registry variables or secrets are needed, and no successful local/privkeyio tagAndRelease run is required. Publication is validated in the Start9-Community fork.
acceptance_criteria: privkeyio tagAndRelease.yml stays untouched and matches the reference Start9Labs workflow so the Start9-Community fork inherits it cleanly; publication is validated in the Start9-Community fork (its Tag and Release runs are green and publishing via Start9 org secrets); no privkeyio repo variables, secrets, or successful privkeyio tagAndRelease run are required.
notes:
Investigated 2026-08-05 (post PR#13 merge). Merge run 31043946365 failed identically: 'tag' job -> 'Check production registry' step, exit 38. Repo has ZERO variables and only DEV_KEY secret (S3_ACCESS_KEY, S3_SECRET_KEY, REFERENCE_REGISTRY, RELEASE_REGISTRY, S3_S9PKS_BASE_URL all unset). Cannot read/set org-level config (HTTP 403, not org admin).

KEY FINDING — precedent contradicts the 'make privkeyio publish' framing: sibling privkeyio/wisp-startos (already in Start9-Community) has tagAndRelease FAILING on every master push (runs 28210162686, 27923483048, 27873946968 — all 12s, same exit). wisp still ships fine because publishing happens in the Start9-Community FORK's CI (Start9 org secrets), not in privkeyio. wisp PR#1 that landed came FROM Start9-Community. keep-startos has no Tag and Release workflow at all.

DECISION NEEDED (blocked on human/org-admin):
 (A) If privkeyio should self-publish to privkey's own registry: need the actual REFERENCE_REGISTRY, RELEASE_REGISTRY, S3_S9PKS_BASE_URL URLs + S3_ACCESS_KEY/S3_SECRET_KEY values from Kyle to set as repo vars/secrets. Cannot proceed without them (will not fabricate).
 (B) If publishing is Start9-Community's job (wisp model): privkeyio tagAndRelease is vestigial; the fix is to stop it erroring on every push (e.g. guard the registry pre-check to skip cleanly when unconfigured) rather than wiring real secrets. This also unblocks j8e via the fork, not via privkeyio CI.
Recommend confirming model with Kyle/Start9 before writing any config.
RESOLVED 2026-08-05 — no change needed (by design). Confirmed with Kyle: Start9-Community fork model. Evidence: Start9-Community/wisp-startos is a fork of privkeyio/wisp-startos with the SAME workflow files (build.yml, release.yml, tagAndRelease.yml) and its Tag and Release runs are GREEN and publishing (runs 30164216843, 30149129096, 30071877794) because Start9's org has the secrets/vars. privkeyio/wisp's own tagAndRelease fails 12s on every push harmlessly and that package is already accepted. Therefore privkeyio's exit-38 is expected: we are NOT the publisher; the fork is. tagAndRelease.yml must stay untouched so the fork inherits and publishes — removing/fail-softing it would break the fork's publish and diverge from the reference workflow Start9 diffs against. Real publish acceptance happens in the fork (j8e). Considered-and-rejected: silencing the red check on privkeyio master (cosmetic; wisp lives with it; divergence risk not worth it).
close_reason: By design — Start9-Community fork model. privkeyio is not the publisher; the fork (with Start9 org secrets) publishes via the same inherited workflow, exactly as accepted for wisp-startos. No repo vars/secrets to set here; workflow must stay untouched.

title: Pin buzz relay image by digest instead of :main
description: ghcr.io/block/buzz:main is a mutable tag, so builds are non-reproducible and the s9pk version encodes nothing about which upstream commit is inside. Pin to the OCI image index digest (covers both amd64+arm64) and record the upstream commit. First verify start-cli 0.4.0-beta.9 accepts an @sha256: reference in dockerTag.
notes: VERIFIED: start-cli 0.4.0-beta.9 accepts 'ghcr.io/block/buzz@sha256:<index-digest>' in dockerTag. Both x86 and arm pack successfully from a single OCI index digest. Initial verification used intermediate digest 3f8d3ff5 (upstream commit 651f637); the FINAL pinned digest is fd837f78 (upstream commit e341b09, relay 0.2.0) — see close_reason and startos/manifest/index.ts. Gotcha: building both arches sequentially in one local docker store fails on the 2nd with 'cannot overwrite digest' -- docker digest refs are immutable, so the 1st arch claims ref->image-id and the 2nd can't remap it. Fix locally: docker rmi the first arch's image between builds. CI unaffected: build.yml/release.yml fan out one runner per target (arm on native ubuntu-24.04-arm), so each arch gets a clean docker store. Also found: packed s9pk manifest reports source='packed' and does NOT record the source digest, so provenance must live in release notes + git.
close_reason: Pinned relay image by digest sha256:fd837f78 (upstream e341b09, relay 0.2.0) and set package version 0.2.0:0. Verified both arches pack. Docs updated; no :main refs remain.

title: Add community host + owner pubkey config; set RELAY_URL/RELAY_OWNER_PUBKEY
description: Relay 404s 'no community is configured for this host' at profile creation because relayEnv never sets RELAY_URL, so the community auto-seeds for localhost:3000 instead of the public host. Add two required fields to the existing Config action: Community Host (e.g. buzz1.privkey.io) and Owner Pubkey (accept npub1... or 64-hex, decode npub to hex). Persist to store.json and wire into relayEnv: RELAY_URL=wss://<host>, RELAY_OWNER_PUBKEY=<hex>, plus host-derived BUZZ_DOMAIN/media/CORS as appropriate. Verified root cause via upstream main.rs:232 ensure_configured_community(host) seeded from RELAY_URL.

title: Smoke test on-box: netns assumption, add-community flow, relay grace period
description:
Three things could not be verified statically and need a real StartOS box (local images are arm64, target is amd64).

1. All inter-daemon addressing assumes subcontainers share a network namespace so compose DNS names collapse to 127.0.0.1. Neither the SDK types nor sources document netns semantics, and sibling packages are all single-container. If wrong, nothing connects.
2. BUZZ_REQUIRE_AUTH_TOKEN=true was enabled (see the relay identity key fix). Auth is NIP-98 per-request signed events, which Buzz Desktop speaks, but the set of auth-exempt routes was not enumerated. If Buzz Desktop probes any REST endpoint unauthenticated during add-community, that probe now 401s. Highest-risk behavioral change to confirm.
3. Relay ready gracePeriod is 60s, but first boot runs migrations (BUZZ_AUTO_MIGRATE=true) plus the git conformance probe. May flip the UI red while still legitimately starting.
notes: ON-BOX E2E PASSED 2026-07-24. Relay verified serving real traffic: curl -vk https://<lan>:51977/_readiness -> 200 {"status":"ready"} through the StartOS TLS proxy. 'Add Community: Load failed' in Buzz Desktop was NOT our package and NOT the auth token -- it is client-side TLS trust: cert CN=localhost/O=Start9 issued by StartOS Local Intermediate CA; desktop lacks the StartOS root CA (curl -v without -k fails code 60, with -k succeeds). Relay logged zero traffic from the attempt = request never passed the TLS handshake, consistent with WebKit 'Load failed' (not a 401). Fix is desktop-side: install StartOS root CA into /usr/local/share/ca-certificates + update-ca-certificates (WebKitGTK reads system store). BUZZ_REQUIRE_AUTH_TOKEN=true exonerated. All smoke-test unknowns (netns, grace period, relay key, community endpoint) now confirmed good.
close_reason: Full on-box e2e PASSED 2026-07-24. After trusting the StartOS root CA on the desktop, Buzz Desktop added the community cleanly and proceeded to username/onboarding. Confirms: netns 127.0.0.1 wiring, relay grace period, stable relay identity (no dev-key warning), community endpoint, AND BUZZ_REQUIRE_AUTH_TOKEN=true (add succeeded with it enabled). Package works end to end.

title: Relay holds MinIO root credentials instead of a scoped service account
description: MINIO_ROOT_USER/MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD on the minio daemon are the same values passed to the relay as BUZZ_S3_ACCESS_KEY/BUZZ_S3_SECRET_KEY. A relay compromise therefore yields full MinIO admin (all buckets, admin API, user creation) rather than scoped access to the single media bucket. minio-init already runs mc, so it can provision a service account scoped to the bucket and hand those keys to the relay instead. See startos/main.ts minio daemon and relayEnv.
close_reason: Fixed in 19bb7ab and verified on-box 2026-07-25: minio-init mints a bucket-scoped MinIO service account (svcacct, inline policy confined to the media bucket) using root only at init; relay runs with s3RelayAccessKey/Secret, never root. Log confirms svcacct created and 'Media storage connected' with the scoped keys — a relay compromise is now confined to the single media bucket.

title: Changing s3Bucket orphans all previously uploaded media
description: The config action allows s3Bucket to be edited at any time. On next start minio-init creates the new bucket (mc mb --ignore-existing) and relayEnv points BUZZ_S3_BUCKET at it, leaving every previously uploaded object stranded in the old bucket with no migration path. The only warning is the generic 'Changes take effect the next time Buzz Relay starts.' Either make s3Bucket install-time-only, or warn explicitly that existing media becomes unreachable. See startos/actions/config.ts and startos/main.ts relayEnv.
close_reason: Mitigated in 08530ea: the s3Bucket config field now carries an explicit warning + expanded description that changing the media bucket orphans all previously uploaded media (files stay in the old bucket, no auto-migration). i18n added across all five languages. Admin is now clearly warned before making the change; not making the field install-time-only since a deliberate reset is a valid use.

title: Relay :3000 interface + clearnet TLS for buzz.privkey.io
description: Buzz Desktop needs publicly-trusted wss cert. Prefer StartOS clearnet -> buzz.privkey.io. Alt: VPS Caddy. Health check :8080/_readiness.
notes:
Note 2026-07-24: LAN add works today WITHOUT clearnet by installing the StartOS root CA on the client machine (system store; WebKitGTK/Tauri-based Buzz Desktop reads it -> add succeeded). Clearnet buzz.privkey.io still wanted so remote clients / mobile don't need manual CA trust. StartOS TLS proxy already terminates TLS on the LAN interface (cert CN=localhost, SAN matches the IP), so this task is really about a publicly-trusted cert + stable hostname, not TLS termination itself.

Verified 2026-07-24: https://buzz1.privkey.io/_readiness returns HTTP 200 {"status":"ready"}. TLS cert CN=buzz1.privkey.io issued by Let's Encrypt (publicly-trusted, verify ok), SAN matches. CORS access-control-allow-origin: * present. Path: client :443 -> VPS Caddy (LE termination) -> box :51977 (StartOS TLS) -> relay :3000. A record buzz1.privkey.io -> 172.235.145.194 (same VPS as relay1). Satisfies publicly-trusted cert + stable hostname goal; remaining is Buzz Desktop e2e add from a client without StartOS CA (issue e38).
close_reason: Verified: https://buzz1.privkey.io publicly-trusted (Let's Encrypt) clearnet endpoint works; Buzz Desktop added the community over wss://buzz1.privkey.io from a client and signed in successfully. Publicly-trusted cert + stable hostname goal met.

title: Build .s9pk, install on box, e2e test in Buzz Desktop
description: start-sdk build -> install -> add wss://buzz.privkey.io as community; verify channels/DMs/media(MinIO/Blossom)/git; confirm backup/restore survives data.
notes:
VERIFIED on-box 2026-07-25 (build cb582bc, branch feature/chown-sentinel) on snappy-winds (StartOS 0.4).

CHANNELS/MEDIA (earlier): signed in over wss://buzz1.privkey.io, default channels + 3 agents, channel message, agent DM, photo upload (MinIO/Blossom round-trip).

GIT BEHAVIOR: relay startup log 'git object-store backend admitted: A3 conformance probe passed' (race_width=32, race_rounds=3) against BUZZ_GIT_REPO_PATH=/data/git. Criterion met.

BACKUP/RESTORE SURVIVES DATA: full cycle exercised (create backup -> uninstall -> restore from backup). After restore the relay came up healthy as uid 1000 on originally-root-owned /data (proves the feature/chown-sentinel fix: postRestore drops /data/.chowned, prepare-data re-chowns). Evidence via nsenter into StartOS runtime + psql: events table restored intact — 13 kind-0 profiles, 13 kind-9 channel messages, 39000/39001/39002 group metadata/admins/members, reactions, deletions. Redis AOF loaded, MinIO 'Media storage connected', git probe passed, all generated secrets + relay identity survived. _readiness HTTP 200; NIP-11 doc 200 with Host: buzz1.privkey.io. Criterion met.

DMs: NOT relay-stored — zero kind 4/13/14/1059 events and no DM table; NIP-17 gift-wraps route to participants' personal inbox relays, out of this package's scope. Empty DM history after restore is expected, not data loss.

GOTCHA (filed separately): uninstall/reinstall wiped the Buzz Relay clearnet Domain (buzz1.privkey.io) + reassigned the StartOS interface port (51977->60723), breaking external reachability until the Public/Domain/LetsEncrypt interface was re-added on the service (which re-registered the start-tunnel automatic port). Not a package defect.
close_reason: Verified end-to-end on-box (build cb582bc): both previously-unverified criteria confirmed. Git behavior — A3 conformance probe passed on /data/git. Backup/restore survives data — full backup->uninstall->restore cycle; relay came up healthy as uid 1000 on restored root-owned /data (feature/chown-sentinel fix working), events table intact (profiles/channels/groups/reactions), redis+MinIO+git+secrets all restored, _readiness 200. DMs confirmed out of scope (not relay-stored). External reachability restored by re-adding clearnet domain (see separate gotcha issue).

title: Surface StartOS-side diagnostics (properties): wss URL, configured host, cert/interface state
description: Buzz Desktop has zero logging and collapses TLS failures and closed ports both to 'could not connect to relay', and a host miss to 'relay returned 404' (verified in j8e). The client cannot tell the operator why 'add community' failed. Compensate from the StartOS side: expose properties/health showing the exact wss:// URL to paste into Buzz Desktop, the currently-seeded Community Host, and whether a clearnet ACME cert is active on the interface — turning the client's silent failures into visible, actionable state.
notes:
Implemented 2026-08-05 (validated: tsc --noEmit clean, ncc build clean). New action startos/actions/diagnostics.ts (withoutInput, allowedStatuses 'any'), registered in actions/index.ts. Surfaces 4 fields as a result group:
 (1) 'Add This Community in Buzz Desktop' — authoritative wss://<activeHost> (boundHost ?? communityHost), copyable; or 'Not configured' prompt.
 (2) 'Community Host' — configured host + lock state (locked/bound vs not-yet-started/editable vs Not set).
 (3) 'Public Domains on Interface' — public domains actually attached to the exported 'ui' interface, read via sdk.host.getOwn(effects,'ui-multi').bindings[relayPort].interfaces['ui'].addressInfo.public.filter({kind:'domain'}).format('url'). A public domain here == StartOS is managing a clearnet cert the webpki-only client trusts.
 (4) 'Connection Readiness' — plain verdict: not-set / ready (activeHost in publicDomains) / mismatch (configured host not among attached public domains) / not-ready (no public domain attached — Let's Encrypt + 443 reminder). Turns Buzz Desktop's silent TLS/404 failures into visible actionable state.
i18n: 6 new keys (ids 27-32) added to default.ts + all 4 translation langs (es/de/fr/pl); reuses existing 'Community Host' (19). Not committed — awaiting go-ahead.
Committed 95cdf5d on feature/startos-diagnostics-action; PR #14 opened into master 2026-08-05.

title: Add 'Reset community' destructive action (wipe Postgres + re-seed)
description: Upstream has NO supported way to re-point a community's host (verified in j8e: table communities keyed on UNIQUE lower(host), buzz-admin has no set-host, operator API only transfers ownership). The only re-point path is wiping the Postgres DB and letting the relay re-seed from RELAY_URL on next boot. Expose a guarded StartOS action that clears the postgres volume and re-seeds, so an admin who set the wrong domain can recover turn-key instead of reinstalling. Must warn that this destroys the existing community, members, and NIP-05 handles.
notes:
Implemented 2026-08-05 on branch (uncommitted, pending user go-ahead). New file startos/actions/reset.ts: sdk.Action.withInput 'reset', allowedStatuses 'only-stopped'. Wipes the postgres volume contents (fs.rm children of sdk.volumes.postgres root; ENOENT-tolerant) so the entrypoint re-initdb's and the relay re-seeds its community on next boot, and clears store.boundHost (null) so the Config action unlocks host edits and main.ts rebinds — enabling a domain re-point. Typed confirmation: operator must type the exact bound/community host (case-insensitive) or it throws; throws 'Nothing to reset' when no host configured. Registered in actions/index.ts. Added i18n indices 33-39 to default.ts + es/de/pl/fr in translations.ts. tsc --noEmit and ncc build both green.

SCOPE NOTE: wipes Postgres only (matches issue + j8e-verified mechanism: community keyed in postgres communities table). The relay's git object store (main volume 'git' subpath, nostr events) is left intact — orphaned events aren't served without matching postgres rows, and the common wrong-domain case is caught before real content exists. If a truly blank slate is ever needed, a follow-up could also clear the git subpath (prepare-data recreates it).

title: Add upstream drift-watch workflow for pinned relay digest
description:
Now that the relay image is pinned by digest, nothing notices when upstream moves. Add a scheduled + workflow_dispatch GitHub workflow that resolves ghcr.io/block/buzz:main's digest (anonymous GHCR token -> HEAD /v2/block/buzz/manifests/main -> docker-content-digest), compares it to the digest in startos/manifest/index.ts, and opens a PR when they differ. PR must include the old->new upstream commit range (read org.opencontainers.image.revision from the new index) and a compare link. Open a PR, never auto-merge: tagAndRelease.yml fires on every push to master, so a merged digest bump auto-publishes and therefore also needs a version bump in startos/versions/current.ts.

Current baseline pin: upstream commit e341b09, OCI index digest sha256:fd837f78ec4f8e0a72b1a165db40cd20946eb4773d337e8eff1573f5d3f41b7d (relay crate 0.2.0), shipped as 0.2.0:0. The workflow MUST only open a PR for an upstream revision strictly newer than the pinned one and reject/skip anything equal-or-older, so it can never downgrade the pin. HISTORICAL (do NOT re-propose): commit 651f637 / digest 3f8d3ff5 was an intermediate test pin used while verifying digest support; it predates e341b09 and has since been superseded. The next genuine drift PR ships as 0.2.0:1; before merging on a live community, take a StartOS backup and review the BUZZ_* env-var contract in startos/main.ts:122-155 (a bump may add migrations).
close_reason: Added .github/workflows/drift-watch.yml (committed 9b1f57f)

title: Start9 community submission: await fork of buzz-relay-startos
description:
Submitted buzz-relay-startos to Start9 community registry via email to submissions@start9.com on 2026-07-25 (from William, partner of Kyle). Ask: fork privkeyio/buzz-relay-startos into Start9-Community, same model as wisp-startos. Awaiting Start9 to create the fork and reply with feedback.

Next steps once fork exists:
- Gain pull access on Start9-Community/buzz-relay-startos
- Drive first release via PR into the fork's master (auto-builds to community-beta on merge)
- Give go-ahead to promote beta -> production community registry

Pre-first-merge gates (see qp8, 5ir): first PR merge auto-ships to community-beta, so clear P1s and add a community README before landing the release PR.
design:
TURN-KEY READINESS EVALUATION — Start9 community developer feedback (2026-08-03)

Verbatim feedback (after ~half a day of testing):
"A bit buggy still, outdated information in the buzz repo. Requires a signed SSL
cert (Buzz Desktop doesn't look at the system CA store, so you need a cert like
Let's Encrypt). This wasn't obvious, and had to let an LLM investigate the
upstream source. (Buzz Desktop doesn't have any logging.) It needs a public
domain, but after initial setup you can't add or change domain names, because
the initially created community will be linked to the URL you used. I feel this
is not ready yet to be a turn-key solution for StartOS. Lots of moving parts and
you have to know a bit about how everything works to set it up correctly."

All four claims VERIFIED against block/buzz @ main:

1. TLS: HARD upstream-CLIENT constraint. Buzz Desktop is Tauri; the wss:// relay
   connection is opened in Rust via tokio-tungstenite with feature
   "rustls-tls-webpki-roots" (desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml) -> validates ONLY
   against bundled Mozilla webpki-roots and IGNORES the OS/system trust store.
   No danger_accept_invalid_certs, no add_root_certificate, no NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS
   anywhere in client code. => StartOS .local / .onion / StartOS-private-CA certs
   fail the WS handshake SILENTLY. A publicly-trusted clearnet cert (Let's Encrypt)
   is effectively REQUIRED. The relay itself terminates NO TLS (serves plain
   HTTP/WS on :3000, crates/buzz-relay/src/main.rs); upstream fronts it with Caddy
   auto-Let's-Encrypt. On StartOS this maps to: expose plain :3000 and require the
   admin to attach a clearnet ACME domain to the interface.

2. Community<->domain lock: VERIFIED, no rename path. Relay reads RELAY_URL (NOT
   BUZZ_-prefixed), derives host, and on boot calls ensure_configured_community(host)
   seeding table `communities` (UUID PK, UNIQUE lower(host)). Every request resolves
   by inbound Host header; a miss returns 404 "relay: no community is configured for
   this host" (router.rs). Changing the host 404s all traffic AND seeds a second,
   empty community; NIP-05 handles (local@domain) all break. buzz-admin has NO
   host-change command; operator API only does provision/archive/transfer-ownership.
   Only re-point path = wipe the Postgres DB and re-seed. So RELAY_URL must be
   pinned to the final clearnet domain BEFORE first boot and treated as immutable.

3. Client logging: VERIFIED none. Desktop Tauri backend has no tauri-plugin-log /
   env_logger / tracing-subscriber; RUST_LOG is ignored. Connection errors are
   collapsed to coarse strings — a TLS failure and a refused port BOTH render as
   "relay unreachable: could not connect to relay"; a host miss renders "relay
   returned 404". The app cannot tell the operator why "add community" failed.

4. Public domain: inherent consequence of (1)+(2). Tor-only / LAN-only installs
   cannot complete the desktop "add community" flow.

Upstream docs ARE stale (tester correct): deploy/compose/.env.example lists
BUZZ_DOMAIN and BUZZ_MEDIA_SERVER_DOMAIN which the relay never reads (Caddy-only);
compose still defaults BUZZ_IMAGE to mutable :main. Env rename gotcha:
BUZZ_REPLICA_HEAD_MAX_AGE_SECS -> BUZZ_REPLICA_READ_MAX_AGE_MS is now a hard
startup error if the old name is set.

VERDICT: The package's daemon stack is sound; the readiness gap is UX/onboarding
around two hard upstream constraints (webpki-only client trust; immutable host).
Cannot be made fully "click-install" while the client ignores non-webpki CAs and
lacks a host-rename path. Best achievable now = "documented + guard-railed": make
the mandatory clearnet-ACME-domain + set-host-before-first-boot flow impossible to
get wrong, and make failures visible from the StartOS side since the client is silent.

WHAT WE CAN DO IN THE PACKAGE (follow-up issues filed):
- Onboarding/instructions: state up front that a PUBLIC clearnet domain with a
  Let's Encrypt cert is REQUIRED (Tor/.local won't work), and that Community Host
  must be set to exactly that domain BEFORE first start and is permanent.
- "Reset community" destructive action: wipe Postgres volume + re-seed, so a wrong
  host is recoverable turn-key instead of requiring a full reinstall.
- StartOS-side diagnostics (properties): surface the exact wss:// URL to add, the
  configured host, and cert/interface state — the only visibility available since
  the client logs nothing.
- Strengthen the immutability warning already in the config action.

WHAT NEEDS UPSTREAM (file with block/buzz; would unlock true turn-key):
- Desktop: honor OS/custom CA (rustls-platform-verifier) or a custom-CA opt-in ->
  would let StartOS's own CA / .local work with NO public domain.
- Desktop: minimal connection logging so failures are diagnosable.
- Relay/admin: a supported community host re-point (buzz-admin set-host + NIP-05
  rebind) so the domain isn't a one-shot decision.
notes:
Start9 answers (2026-08-05, package-dev room):
Q1 public-domain requirement: ACCEPTED as a valid package requirement. Verbatim: 'If the package requires a public domain, then that's what it requires. Synapse (Matrix) requires this, and it's on the Start9 Registry. It's rare though. The only times we've seen this requirement is if the host itself is part of a network identifier, like it is with Synapse or Mastodon.' => buzz's host-as-network-identifier (communities keyed on host) is exactly the sanctioned case. Not a blocker for registry inclusion.
Q2 beta->production promotion: DEVELOPER'S CALL, not Start9-gated. Verbatim: 'For community services, they go to production when the developer says they are tested and good to go. Start9 only gates access to beta.' => No external turn-key bar to clear for production; we self-certify when tested/good. Start9 only controls beta access (via the fork). The 'is it turn-key enough' verdict is ours to make, not theirs.

title: Reinstall/restore wipes Buzz Relay clearnet domain + reassigns interface port, breaking external access
description: After an uninstall+restore (or reinstall) of the Buzz Relay service on StartOS, external clearnet access via wss://buzz1.privkey.io breaks even though the relay is fully healthy on-box (_readiness 200, NIP-11 200 with correct Host header). Two things reset on reinstall: (1) StartOS reassigns the service TLS interface port (observed 51977 -> 60723), and (2) the service's Public/Domain (Let's Encrypt) clearnet interface for buzz1.privkey.io is removed, so the box no longer SNI-routes buzz1 to the relay and start-tunnel no longer has an automatic published port for it. Observed 2026-07-25 during e38 restore verification: buzz1.privkey.io was absent from start-tunnel Published Ports (both Manual and Automatic tables). Clearnet is handled by Start9 start-tunnel (SNI passthrough External 443 -> box ingress; the box routes by hostname), NOT the service port directly.
acceptance_criteria: Restore runbook documents the post-restore step; ideally the clearnet domain survives restore or is auto-re-registered.
notes:
INVESTIGATION 2026-07-25: clearnet domain CANNOT be made to survive restore from the package side. It is host-level StartOS config (interface<->domain via start-tunnel), user-specific (the operator's own domain), and the SDK exposes no interface API to declare a clearnet/ACME domain — setupInterfaces/createInterface/bindPort/MultiHost only bind ports (see startos/interfaces.ts). The package backup is ofVolumes only (backups.ts), which correctly does NOT capture a domain choice. So restore reinstalls package+volumes but cannot recreate the host domain binding. The relay's internal community host DOES survive (store.json -> RELAY_URL/BUZZ_MEDIA_BASE_URL), so only the StartOS clearnet route is lost. Interface port also reassigns on reinstall (51977->60723) but tunnel routes by SNI so that alone is harmless.

RESOLUTION: documented mandatory post-restore step in PLAN.md ('Restore runbook' section) — re-add Public/Domain/Let's Encrypt interface for the host, which re-registers the start-tunnel automatic port. Workaround verified: https://buzz1.privkey.io/_readiness returned 200 immediately after re-adding. Not fixable in package code; closing as documented. Upstream note (optional): StartOS restore not preserving host clearnet-domain bindings is a platform behavior, could be raised with Start9.
close_reason: Investigated: clearnet domain is host-level/user-specific StartOS config with no SDK API to declare it and is correctly not in the volume backup, so it cannot survive restore from the package side. Documented mandatory post-restore re-add step in PLAN.md Restore runbook; workaround verified (readiness 200 after re-adding domain). Not a package defect.

title: prepare-data chowns all of /data on every start
description: The prepare-data oneshot runs 'mkdir -p /data/git && chown -R 1000:1000 /data' unconditionally on every service start. /data/git holds git repositories (BUZZ_GIT_REPO_PATH), so this is O(number of files) and will visibly delay startup as repos grow. Guard it on a sentinel file, or scope the chown to freshly created paths. See startos/main.ts prepare-data oneshot.
close_reason: Guard prepare-data chown behind /data/.chowned sentinel so recursive chown runs once, not every start

title: Implement 4 daemons + minio-init with health-gated ordering
description: postgres healthy -> redis healthy -> minio healthy -> minio-init completes -> relay. Model on synapse Postgres bundling.
close_reason: Implemented postgres/redis/minio/relay daemons + minio-init and prepare-data oneshots with health-gated ordering in startos/main.ts

title: Map env vars; rewire service hostnames to localhost
description: compose uses postgres/redis/minio DNS; in-package daemons share localhost -> 127.0.0.1:5432/6379/9000. Set BUZZ_AUTO_MIGRATE=true.

title: Diagnostics: run readiness and host/domain status strings through i18n()
description: In startos/actions/diagnostics.ts the four readiness strings and the two host/domain status strings (e.g. '${communityHost} (locked — bound at first start)', the readiness sentences) are built with template literals and are not run through i18n(), so they stay English-only while surrounding labels are translated. UX/consistency nit. Fixing requires registering parameterized strings in the i18n dicts across all languages.

title: Diagnostics: harden host/domain exact-match against URL.hostname suffix drift
description: startos/actions/diagnostics.ts:41 uses publicDomains.includes(activeHost), an exact string match between the config-derived host and URL.hostname. Correct today (both lowercased at source; degrades to Mismatch branch gracefully), but relies on the OS-managed domain's URL.hostname being the bare domain with no suffix. Follow-up: make the comparison robust to suffix/normalization drift so a valid domain never produces a spurious Mismatch verdict.

title: File upstream feature requests with block/buzz to unlock true turn-key
description: Two package-side guard-rails (see j8e) only paper over hard upstream-client constraints. File issues with github.com/block/buzz: (1) Desktop should honor the OS trust store / offer a custom-CA opt-in (rustls-platform-verifier instead of webpki-roots-only) — this would let StartOS's own CA / .local work with NO public domain, the single biggest turn-key unlock; (2) Desktop needs minimal connection/TLS logging so failures are diagnosable; (3) relay/buzz-admin needs a supported community host re-point (set-host + NIP-05 rebind) so the domain isn't a one-shot irreversible decision. Also note upstream doc drift: .env.example lists BUZZ_DOMAIN/BUZZ_MEDIA_SERVER_DOMAIN the relay never reads, and still defaults BUZZ_IMAGE to mutable :main.

title: Postgres logs partition-overlap ERRORs during buzz migrations (non-fatal)
description: On first boot, buzz DB migrations emit several postgres ERRORs like: partition 'events_p2026_07' would overlap partition 'events_p_future'. Same for delivery_log. These are idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS partition attempts colliding with an existing catch-all _p_future partition. Relay logs 'Database migrations complete' immediately after and boots fully, so non-fatal. Appears to be an upstream buzz migration quirk (monthly partitions vs a future catch-all), not caused by this package. Track in case it signals a real gap in partition coverage later.

title: Confirm BUZZ_GIT_CONFORMANCE_PROBE=true is intended for production
description: relayEnv sets BUZZ_GIT_CONFORMANCE_PROBE=true, which gates startup on a git object-store conformance probe ('A3 gate', with BUZZ_GIT_PROBE_WRITERS/BUZZ_GIT_PROBE_ROUNDS tuning knobs). This runs on every start and is pure startup latency if it is really an upstream CI gate rather than a production setting. Confirm against upstream deploy/compose and drop it if not needed. See startos/main.ts relayEnv.
notes: Observed on-box 2026-07-24: BUZZ_GIT_CONFORMANCE_PROBE=true runs on every boot ('running git object-store conformance probe (A3 gate)' race_width=32 race_rounds=3 -> 'A3 conformance probe passed', transport_drops=2). Cost ~7s of startup (20:58:56 -> 20:59:03), and the relay does not bind :3000/:8080 until it passes. Non-fatal transport-drop WARNs during the probe are expected. Decide whether that gate belongs in production or was an upstream CI knob; if kept, the relay gracePeriod must stay >= probe time.
close_reason: Confirmed BUZZ_GIT_CONFORMANCE_PROBE=true is the upstream production default (deploy/compose defaults it to true), not a CI-only knob. Kept as-is; relay gracePeriod (60s) already exceeds the ~7s probe. Added a comment in main.ts documenting the decision.

title: Redis password passed in argv for server and health check
description: redis-server is started with --requirepass <password> and the health check runs 'redis-cli -a <password> ping', so the password is visible in the process list within the container and redis-cli emits a security warning to stderr on every poll. Contained to the package, but avoidable: use a redis config file for the server and REDISCLI_AUTH for the health check. See startos/main.ts redis daemon.
close_reason: Redis server now reads requirepass from /tmp/redis.conf written from an env var (not argv), and the health check reads it into REDISCLI_AUTH — password stays off the process list and the redis-cli -a stderr warning is gone. tsc --noEmit passes.
